x.ASV: Jehovah reigneth; let the peoples tremble: He sitteth above the cherubim; let the earth be moved.
x.Darby: Jehovah reigneth: let the peoples tremble. He sitteth [between the] cherubim: let the earth be moved.
x.KJV: The Lord reigneth; let the people tremble: he sitteth between the cherubims; let the earth be moved.
x.YLT: Jehovah hath reigned, peoples tremble, The Inhabitant of the cherubs, the earth shaketh.

nt: יְהוָ֣ה מָ֭לָךְ יִרְגְּז֣וּ עַמִּ֑ים יֹשֵׁ֥ב כְּ֝רוּבִ֗ים תָּנ֥וּט הָ⁠אָֽרֶץ

If it would be helpful in your language, you could move the phrase **let the peoples tremble** so that it does not interrupt the larger sentence. Alternate translation: [Yahweh reigns, sitting above the cherubs; let the peoples tremble and let the earth quake]

If it would be helpful, you could explain in the text or a footnote that Yahweh is pictured here as sitting above the cherubs that are on the lid of the ark of the covenant, which is in his temple in Jerusalem. The biblical writers often spoke of the ark of the covenant as if it were Yahweh’s footstool upon which he rested his feet as he sat on his throne in heaven above. Alternate translation: [he sits on his throne above the cherubs on the ark of the covenant]

x.ASV: Jehovah is great in Zion; And he is high above all the peoples.
x.Darby: Jehovah is great in Zion, and he is high above all the peoples.
x.KJV: The Lord is great in Zion; and he is high above all the people.
x.YLT: Jehovah in Zion is great, And high He is over all the peoples.

nt: By **is great**, the psalmist means that Yahweh is powerful and mighty as a ruler. You could indicate this explicitly in your translation if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [is a powerful ruler]

The psalmist is speaking as if Yahweh were actually **high above** all the peoples in a physical sense. He means that Yahweh powerfully rules over all the peoples. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and he powerfully rules over]

x.ASV: Let them praise thy great and terrible name: Holy is he.
x.Darby: They shall praise thy great and terrible name, — it is holy! —
x.KJV: Let them praise thy great and terrible name; for it is holy.
x.YLT: They praise Thy name, `Great, and fearful, holy it is.'

nt: The psalmist is using the term **name** to represent who Yahweh is or to refer to Yahweh’s reputation. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [you, who are great and fearsome]

In this psalm, the psalmist switches between talking about Yahweh in the third person and addressing him in second person. If it would be helpful in your language, you could translate this verse in the third person. Alternate translation: [his great and fearsome name]

x.ASV: The king’s strength also loveth justice; Thou dost establish equity; Thou executest justice and righteousness in Jacob.
x.Darby: And the strength of the king that loveth justice. Thou hast established equity: it is thou that executest judgment and righteousness in Jacob.
x.KJV: The king’s strength also loveth judgment; thou dost establish equity, thou executest judgment and righteousness in Jacob.
x.YLT: And the strength of the king Hath loved judgment, Thou--Thou hast established uprightness; Judgment and righteousness in Jacob, Thou--Thou hast done.

nt: If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **strength**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [And the king is strong]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **justice**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [he loves doing what is just]

The psalmist is stating the pronoun **you** separately, even though the verb translated as **you have established** already includes this meaning. He is doing that to emphasize that Yahweh is the one who has established fairness. If a speaker of your language would use an explicit pronoun for the same purpose, you may want to use that construction in your translation. If not, your language may have other ways of showing the meaning here. Alternate translation: [you are the one who has established fairness]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **fairness**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [you have given us laws that are fair]

The psalmist is stating the pronoun **you** separately, even though the verb translated as **you have done** already includes this meaning. He is doing that to emphasize that Yahweh is the one who has done justice and righteousness. If a speaker of your language would use an explicit pronoun for the same purpose, you may want to use that construction in your translation. If not, your language may have other ways of showing the meaning here. Alternate translation: [you are the one who has done justice and righteousness]

If your language does not use abstract nouns for the ideas of **justice** and **righteousness**, you could express the same ideas in other ways. Alternate translation: [everything that you have done for Jacob is just and right]

By **in Jacob**, the psalmist means in the land of Israel. You could indicate this explicitly in your translation if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [in the land of Israel]

x.ASV: Exalt ye Jehovah our God, And worship at his footstool: Holy is he.
x.Darby: Exalt Jehovah ourGod, and worship at his footstool. He is holy!
x.KJV: Exalt ye the Lord our God, and worship at his footstool; for he is holy.
x.YLT: Exalt ye Jehovah our God, And bow yourselves at His footstool, holy is He.

nt: The command forms in this verse and verse 9 are plural, so use that form if your language marks that distinction.

If it would be helpful, you could explain in the text or a footnote that the psalmist is continuing to picture Yahweh as sitting above the ark of the covenant, which is in his temple in Jerusalem. Alternate translation: [and worship Yahweh before his throne in the temple]

x.ASV: Moses and Aaron among his priests, And Samuel among them that call upon his name; They called upon Jehovah, and he answered them.
x.Darby: Moses and Aaron among his priests, and Samuel among them that call upon his name: they called unto Jehovah, and he answered them.
x.KJV: Moses and Aaron among his priests, and Samuel among them that call upon his name; they called upon the Lord, and he answered them.
x.YLT: Moses and Aaron among His priests, And Samuel among those proclaiming His name. They are calling unto Jehovah, And He doth answer them.

nt: Here, **calling his name** represents praying to God or calling out to him. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [was among those calling out to him]

The psalmist is stating the pronoun **he** separately, even though the verb translated as **answered** already includes this meaning. He is doing that to emphasize that Yahweh himself responded to Moses, Aaron, and Samuel. If a speaker of your language would use an explicit pronoun for the same purpose, you may want to use that construction in your translation. If not, your language may have other ways of showing the meaning here. Alternate translation: [and he himself answered them]

By **he answered them**, the psalmist means that God helped Moses, Aaron, and Samuel when they called out to him for assistance. You could indicate this explicitly in your translation if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [he helped them]

x.ASV: He spake unto them in the pillar of cloud: They kept his testimonies, And the statute that he gave them.
x.Darby: He spoke unto them in the pillar of cloud: they kept his testimonies, and the statute that he gave them.
x.KJV: He spake unto them in the cloudy pillar: they kept his testimonies, and the ordinance that he gave them.
x.YLT: In a pillar of cloud He speaketh unto them, They have kept His testimonies, And the statute He hath given to them.

nt: The pronoun **them** refers to Moses and Aaron mentioned in the previous verse, since they were the ones whom Yahweh spoke to out of the cloud. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [he spoke to Moses and Aaron]

The pronoun **They** probably includes Samuel here, along with Moses and Aaron, since Yahweh also spoke directly to him and he obeyed. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [Moses, Aaron, and Samuel]

x.ASV: Thou answeredst them, O Jehovah our God: Thou wast a God that forgavest them, Though thou tookest vengeance of their doings.
x.Darby: Jehovah, ourGod, thou answeredst them: a forgivingGod wast thou unto them, though thou tookest vengeance of their doings.
x.KJV: Thou answeredst them, O Lord our God: thou wast a God that forgavest them, though thou tookest vengeance of their inventions.
x.YLT: O Jehovah, our God, Thou hast afflicted them, A God forgiving Thou hast been to them, And taking vengeance on their actions.

nt: The psalmist is using this possessive form to mean the God whom the people worship. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [the God whom we worship]

The psalmist is stating the pronoun **you** separately, even though the verb translated as **you answered** already includes this meaning. He is doing that to emphasize that God himself personally answered them. If a speaker of your language would use an explicit pronoun for the same purpose, you may want to use that construction in your translation. If not, your language may have other ways of showing the meaning here. Alternate translation: [you answered them yourself]
The pronoun **them** refers to Moses, Aaron, and Samuel. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [you answered Moses, Aaron, and Samuel]

The implication is that God answered Moses, Aaron, and Samuel by helping them when they called out to him in times of need. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [you helped them]

Here the psalmist assumes that readers will know that **their deeds** refers to sinful or wrongful actions. You could say that explicitly if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [their sinful deeds]

x.ASV: Exalt ye Jehovah our God, And worship at his holy hill; For Jehovah our God is holy.
x.Darby: Exalt Jehovah ourGod, and worship at the hill of his holiness; for holy is Jehovah ourGod.
x.KJV: Exalt the Lord our God, and worship at his holy hill; for the Lord our God is holy.
x.YLT: Exalt ye Jehovah our God, And bow yourselves at His holy hill, For holy is Jehovah our God!

nt: The psalmist is using this possessive form to mean the God whom the people worship. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [the God whom we worship]

The psalmist is using the possessive form to describe **the hill** that is characterized by **his holiness**. If a speaker of your language would not use the possessive form for this, you could express this idea in another way. Alternate translation: [at his holy hill]

By **the hill of his holiness**, the psalmist means the hill where God’s holy temple is located. You could indicate this explicitly in your translation if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [at the hill where his holy temple is located]
